45cb25eac1bda5913bc330fabf483e71d210042f.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech during the 1987 General Election campaign.
Date: 1987-05-28
Immediate context: The internal power dynamics and ideological shift of the Labour Party.

Meaning: To convince voters that electing Labour would mean handing power to extreme left-wing militants, regardless of the moderate appearance of some Labour MPs.

Verification: Verified excerpt
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech of May 28, 1987

469a6ec354b82c67cc085535d5ed8f16086ad66e.source_event: TV Interview for TV-AM Frost on Sunday
469a6ec354b82c67cc085535d5ed8f16086ad66e.text:
Historical context
Occasion: TV Interview for TV-AM Frost on Sunday.
Date: December 30, 1988
Immediate context: The nature of socialism and its impact on individual liberty.

Meaning: Thatcher argues that socialism does not genuinely serve society or ordinary people, but rather functions as an academic, top-down system designed to control individuals. She asserts that people naturally resist such control because they wish to direct their own lives.

Verification: Normalised wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Document 107144

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, PREM19/4408 f48

486ac8259439d7b2857b5accce1e57ee83bce66c.source_event: Letter to Foreign Secretary Douglas Hurd regarding the Bosnian War
486ac8259439d7b2857b5accce1e57ee83bce66c.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Letter to Foreign Secretary Douglas Hurd regarding the Bosnian War.
Date: July 30, 1992
Immediate context: The ongoing atrocities and ethnic cleansing in Bosnia.

Meaning: That moral duty compels the British government and the international community to intervene and stop the violence in the Balkans.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, PREM19/4408 f48

source.title: Hansard, HC Deb 16 April 1986 vol 95 cc875-86

49f8640fda9f890389e594dfdda488f012367be1.source_event: House of Commons Debate on the US Bombing of Libya
49f8640fda9f890389e594dfdda488f012367be1.text:
Historical context
Occasion: House of Commons Debate on the US Bombing of Libya.
Date: 16 April 1986
Immediate context: The psychological tactics of terrorism and the necessity of resisting it despite public fear.

Meaning: Thatcher argued that free societies must not allow the fear generated by terrorism to prevent them from taking decisive military or defensive action. Yielding to such fear would mean the ultimate defeat of a free society.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Hansard, HC Deb 16 April 1986 vol 95 cc875-86

4a3ab5b0d0c9d5222be085ea91e57402fbe2cb71.source_event: First remarks as Prime Minister on the steps of 10 Downing Street
4a3ab5b0d0c9d5222be085ea91e57402fbe2cb71.text:
Historical context
Occasion: First remarks as Prime Minister on the steps of 10 Downing Street.
Date: 1979-05-04
Immediate context: Her guiding principles for the incoming Conservative government.

Meaning: To project a unifying, healing, and optimistic approach to governance after a highly divisive period in British politics.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Document 104078

4ac9c0148408ada0192ebedefab8a0910fbce8bb.source_event: Article for The Sun ('The Britain I Want')
4ac9c0148408ada0192ebedefab8a0910fbce8bb.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Article for The Sun ('The Britain I Want').
Date: May 2, 1979
Immediate context: The balance between state welfare and individual responsibility.

Meaning: A compassionate society must provide a safety net for the vulnerable, but it must also demand self-reliance and grant economic freedom to those capable of working.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Document 103980

4b3a72437e90fda155fde2ce95e49a0def5faaed.source_event: Article titled 'The Moral Basis of a Free Society' published in the Daily Telegraph
4b3a72437e90fda155fde2ce95e49a0def5faaed.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Article titled 'The Moral Basis of a Free Society' published in the Daily Telegraph.
Date: May 16, 1978
Immediate context: The distinction between genuine community duty and state-mandated welfare.

Meaning: Thatcher argued that fulfilling one's duty to the community and caring for others should be a matter of personal moral choice rather than something delegated to and enforced by a coercive state bureaucracy.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Document 103687

4b53af75f4bf9c618f8705d104bebb7ea4708887.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech at a Polish University.
Date: October 3, 1991
Immediate context: The nature and value of freedom of discussion.

Meaning: True freedom of discussion requires mutual respect, active listening, and open debate, which collectively advance human knowledge.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

4c135c053d61ff9441b6aed5b77213967f434892.text:
Historical context
Source event: 1979 General Election Campaign (attributed).
Date: 1979 (attributed)
Immediate context: The severe disruptions and public suffering caused by the trade union strikes during the winter of 1978-1979.

Meaning: That the unchecked power of trade unions has led to unacceptable societal cruelty, necessitating fundamental conservative reforms to restore order.

Verification: Exact wording not verified
Source: Attribution record: mdpi.com

source.title: Conservative Party television broadcast during the 'Winter of Discontent'

4c950f10a42b15df1d14e37a5f431c0f20f99ef5.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Conservative Party television broadcast.
Date: January 17, 1979
Immediate context: National unity and the disruptive power of trade unions.

Meaning: Britain must overcome the divisive strikes and excessive union power to restore national cohesion, or risk losing its identity and viability as a nation.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Conservative Party television broadcast during the 'Winter of Discontent'

4c9b51eb69875a896e83f9e4a07655ad8c1de120.source_event: Speech to Conservative Rally in Cardiff
4c9b51eb69875a896e83f9e4a07655ad8c1de120.text:
Historical context
Source event: Speech to Conservative Rally in Cardiff.
Date: April 16, 1979
Immediate context: The role of the state versus individual enterprise.

Meaning: That a powerful, centralized state is inherently unfeeling, whereas individual ambition and entrepreneurship naturally generate broader societal benefits.

Verification: Historical paraphrase
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech to IDU

4c9b5b2d2dd30ba5dc20d850646ca3e897d782d8.source_event: Speech to the inaugural conference of the International Democrat Union (IDU)
4c9b5b2d2dd30ba5dc20d850646ca3e897d782d8.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to the inaugural conference of the International Democrat Union (IDU).
Date: June 24, 1983
Immediate context: The resilience of the desire for freedom in totalitarian regimes, specifically in Eastern Europe.

Meaning: That communist and totalitarian systems are fundamentally unnatural and cannot permanently suppress the human yearning for democratic governance.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech to IDU

4d0ee2952c87bc6d0ef3b344bf5bba3d1b37c488.source_event: TV Interview for LWT Weekend World
4d0ee2952c87bc6d0ef3b344bf5bba3d1b37c488.text:
Historical context
Occasion: TV Interview for LWT Weekend World.
Date: June 5, 1983
Immediate context: Government borrowing and public expenditure.

Meaning: Deficit spending is fundamentally unsustainable and inevitably leads to severe national economic crises.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, 1983 Jun 5

4d226cdd3321371650fcf839f8920a27c3acd283.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Conservative Central Council.
Date: 1987-03-21
Immediate context: The conservative vision of individual freedom and faith in the individual over the state.

Meaning: Empowering individuals rather than relying on state planning leads to a more successful and prosperous country.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

4d506792b4c0d2f9010359557d5eba4a0167478a.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Nicholas Ridley Memorial Lecture.
Date: November 22, 1996
Immediate context: The moral failings inherent in socialism.

Meaning: Socialism appeals to and fosters the worst aspects of human nature by validating them under the guise of moral superiority.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

4d86b60909c026a4a30be158310945742a1c2547.source_event: Speech to Greater London Young Conservatives (Iain Macleod Memorial Lecture)
4d86b60909c026a4a30be158310945742a1c2547.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Greater London Young Conservatives (Iain Macleod Memorial Lecture).
Date: July 4, 1977
Immediate context: The tendency of socialists to unfairly criticize the Victorian era and past generations using modern standards.

Meaning: Conservatives should respect historical achievements and avoid the liberal or socialist mistake of condemning the past based on present-day moral or political standards.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

source.title: Iain Dale (1997), 'As I said to Denis--: the Margaret Thatcher book of quotations'

4e08964fca7fabd939c7be1842bcc25133d0a5d8.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Source event not established.
Date: Unknown
Immediate context: The nature of international trade and national economic competitiveness.

Meaning: Trade occurs naturally when businesses offer desirable, high-quality goods at competitive prices, making political pleading unnecessary.

Verification: Verified excerpt
Source: Iain Dale (1997), 'As I said to Denis--: the Margaret Thatcher book of quotations'

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech to Conservative Party Conference, October 8, 1976

4e255992099e6fbb8794ae0e3e044a12c9f38c26.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Conservative Party Conference.
Date: October 8, 1976
Immediate context: A call to action against the perceived Marxist trajectory of the Labour Party.

Meaning: The Conservative Party must lead a broad national crusade, appealing beyond its traditional base, to prevent socialism from permanently altering the British social order.

Verification: Verified excerpt
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech to Conservative Party Conference, October 8, 1976

4e3084635fd956f139d521bcdf10c484afbf05c5.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Finchley Conservatives.
Date: 1976-01-31
Immediate context: The failures and false promises of nationalising industries under the guise of 'public ownership'.

Meaning: To argue that nationalisation strips the public of actual control and accountability while forcing them to bear the financial burdens of state-run inefficiencies.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: margaretthatcher.org/document/102947

4e92014dc14fd9cce562099b03ccfdf480fd5909.source_event: Speech to the Conservative Party Conference
4e92014dc14fd9cce562099b03ccfdf480fd5909.text:
Historical context
Source event: Speech to the Conservative Party Conference.
Date: October 8, 1976
Immediate context: The ideological direction of the Labour Party.

Meaning: That the Labour Party had been captured by its radical left wing and was pursuing a Marxist agenda dangerous to British freedom and prosperity.

Verification: Composite wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

4ea4e926c5aee56df329a14e46212e30060e553e.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Conservative Central Council.
Date: March 15, 1975
Immediate context: The Conservative Party's core beliefs regarding the distribution of power and property ownership.

Meaning: Conservatism empowers individuals through property ownership and personal choice, whereas Socialism centralizes control and restricts freedom.

Verification: Normalised wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation, Document 102655

4f5e783f4957dc615742df2b827214e539a5123a.text:
Historical context
Occasion: The Downing Street Years (Memoir).
Date: 1993
Immediate context: The relationship between trade union power and unemployment levels.

Meaning: Trade unions cause unemployment by forcing wages above market clearing levels, which makes domestic goods uncompetitive and destroys jobs.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Page 272

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech of September 9, 1991, 'Defending Truth' section.

4f657d67183044e12ea9fa4bab713121f1b114c4.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech on Democracy and Freedom.
Date: September 9, 1991
Immediate context: The fundamental incompatibility between truth and Communist rule.

Meaning: Totalitarian regimes rely entirely on the suppression of truth to maintain power, making the free flow of information their greatest existential threat.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech of September 9, 1991, 'Defending Truth' section.

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, document dated April 28, 1988

4ffa3d1db4201e7a9302c3e90098a6142747fc65.source_event: Speech or public remarks defending individualism and economic policy
4ffa3d1db4201e7a9302c3e90098a6142747fc65.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech or public remarks defending individualism and economic policy.
Date: April 28, 1988
Immediate context: The justification for tax cuts and the role of individuals in the economy.

Meaning: Tax cuts are essential to motivate individuals to create wealth, which is the only way a nation can afford to fund public services and social reforms.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, document dated April 28, 1988

5031e014fbb9f27c5e8b13477726933029935c58.source_event: Speech to Scottish Conservative Party Conference
5031e014fbb9f27c5e8b13477726933029935c58.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Scottish Conservative Party Conference.
Date: 1978-05-13
Immediate context: The negative consequences of socialist economic policies on industry and management.

Meaning: Devaluing management and denigrating profits leads to poor industrial management, lack of investment, and ultimately a lack of jobs.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: margaretthatcher.org archive

5112489e69abb6b54d5804a680fa1d2a2d395155.source_event: Speech to the National Press Club
5112489e69abb6b54d5804a680fa1d2a2d395155.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to the National Press Club.
Date: November 5, 1993
Immediate context: The role of the nation-state and the dangers of internationalist consensus.

Meaning: Thatcher argued that a strong nation-state, rather than international organizations or consensus-driven diplomacy, is essential for maintaining peace and freedom.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

source.title: Hansard, House of Commons Debates, July 25, 1979

51346064e36d2597e3cbe635dbe9ff8258b529b5.source_event: Speech to the House of Commons
51346064e36d2597e3cbe635dbe9ff8258b529b5.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to the House of Commons.
Date: July 25, 1979
Immediate context: The proposed use of economic sanctions against South Africa to combat apartheid.

Meaning: Thatcher argued that economic sanctions are counterproductive and would disproportionately harm the very people they were intended to help, specifically black Africans and progressive businesses.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Hansard, House of Commons Debates, July 25, 1979

5189f2683ec11a28cc0507226cff34c24e7341a4.text:
Historical context
Source event: Source event not established.
Date: Unknown
Immediate context: The memory of the Cold War and the preservation of liberty.

Meaning: Forgetting the lessons and sacrifices of the Cold War endangers the future of freedom, as leaders will lack the resolve and understanding required to defend it.

Verification: Exact wording not verified
Source: Attribution record: weirs.com

5239794d7c4ed09128758fc60941d5552cae8ba3.source_event: Article for the News of the World
5239794d7c4ed09128758fc60941d5552cae8ba3.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Article for the News of the World.
Date: April 29, 1979
Immediate context: The Conservative Party's vision for economic revival and individual liberty.

Meaning: Britain's economic decline is caused by socialist state control, and prosperity can only be restored by trusting individuals and removing bureaucratic constraints.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

52f9b9f99f66ff3bc786183803f3a8d682776044.source_event: Private conversation with Sir Anthony Parsons
52f9b9f99f66ff3bc786183803f3a8d682776044.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Private conversation with Sir Anthony Parsons.
Date: 1978
Immediate context: Members of the Conservative Party who still supported consensus politics and compromise.

Meaning: Consensus politics is a betrayal of conservative principles and national interest, requiring a firm ideological break rather than compromise.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Hugo Young, 'One of Us' (1989), p. 193

5357ec1a224ef0998757beda050345d30881d4db.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Article for Hamburger Abendblatt.
Date: May 13, 1978
Immediate context: The need for unity and vigilance among democratic, anti-Marxist parties in Europe.

Meaning: Proponents of freedom must be more dedicated and energetic than their ideological opponents to prevent the spread of Marxism.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation, Document 103683

53699726287c4fed9ef2b086e53cc2938b1fd482.text:
Historical context
Source event: Source event not established.
Date: Unknown
Immediate context: The definition and components of success.

Meaning: Success requires more than just natural talent; it demands hard work and a clear sense of purpose.

Verification: Exact wording not verified
Source: Attribution record: indiatimes.com

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Thatcher MSS (Churchill Archive Centre): THCR

5375f62e3ac4d5c44f8f691b94a9cfc52eb3f2e0.source_event: Speech to the Polish Senate in Warsaw
5375f62e3ac4d5c44f8f691b94a9cfc52eb3f2e0.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to the Polish Senate in Warsaw.
Date: October 3, 1991
Immediate context: The fundamental nature of the Communist Party and its incompatibility with democratic systems.

Meaning: The Communist Party is not a legitimate political entity but a totalitarian apparatus that fuses with and hollows out the state, meaning it must be completely uprooted rather than reformed.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Thatcher MSS (Churchill Archive Centre): THCR

5440b194ff60f3b728644d36cb483d0c23448616.source_event: Statecraft: Strategies for a Changing World (Book)
5440b194ff60f3b728644d36cb483d0c23448616.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Statecraft: Strategies for a Changing World (Book).
Date: 2002
Immediate context: The fundamental nature and viability of the European Union.

Meaning: The European Union is an artificial, top-down construct lacking the organic cultural unity required for a successful state, making its eventual failure inevitable.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Page 359

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation archive, document from May 6, 1978

544b1f58dd541d3840f6eb6dde794b38f1731c40.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech, May 6, 1978.
Date: May 6, 1978
Immediate context: The irrelevance of Marxist class theory to modern society.

Meaning: Thatcher argued that modern workers are citizens of their countries with legal protections and rights, not an oppressed international proletariat. Therefore, Marxist theories based on 19th-century conditions are obsolete.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation archive, document from May 6, 1978

545aee361007f6d7f39394fab1bafb1fd05bc42f.source_event: Speech to Institute of Journalists ('Press Freedom')
545aee361007f6d7f39394fab1bafb1fd05bc42f.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Institute of Journalists ('Press Freedom').
Date: 1978-11-28
Immediate context: The fundamental purpose and value of a free press in a democratic society.

Meaning: A free press is essential not because journalists are perfect, but because independent newspapers serve as a crucial bulwark against state overreach and tyranny.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation, Document 103793 (Speaking Text)

54bcfa6d526fe5de3d3f6db6ee2b1707030258c0.source_event: Speech on the eve of the October 1974 General Election
54bcfa6d526fe5de3d3f6db6ee2b1707030258c0.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech on the eve of the October 1974 General Election.
Date: October 9, 1974
Immediate context: The balance of power between trade unions and the democratically elected government.

Meaning: A democratic system relies on the minority accepting the rule of the elected majority, and no interest group should wield more power than the government.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

54d5a420549526c6b9bc6af7665519325c278239.source_event: Speech to Greater London Young Conservatives (Iain Macleod Memorial Lecture - "Dimensions of Conservatism")
54d5a420549526c6b9bc6af7665519325c278239.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Greater London Young Conservatives (Iain Macleod Memorial Lecture - "Dimensions of Conservatism").
Date: July 4, 1977
Immediate context: The fundamental difference in starting points between Conservative and socialist philosophies.

Meaning: Conservatism is inherently superior because it respects the spiritual uniqueness and individual responsibility of human beings, whereas socialism treats people as mere components to be fitted into a collective societal structure.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Document 103411

5592651c6952bbbec34e0f7ea8ba70584facee50.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Keith Joseph Memorial Lecture.
Date: January 11, 1996
Immediate context: The proper role and limits of the state in society.

Meaning: Government cannot create prosperity or human fulfillment; it can only provide the foundational framework of freedom and rule of law that allows individuals to achieve these things.

Verification: Normalised wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

56ad83fce3f67cb04eaa9bf4baaf858d776971e7.source_event: Speech to the Conservative Party Conference
56ad83fce3f67cb04eaa9bf4baaf858d776971e7.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to the Conservative Party Conference.
Date: October 10, 1975
Immediate context: The ideological trajectory of the Labour Party.

Meaning: The moderate ('mild') faction of the Labour Party is disappearing, leaving only the resentful, extreme socialist ('bitter' and 'Left') faction in control.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Document 102777

source.title: Iain Dale (ed.), 'As I Said to Denis: The Margaret Thatcher Book of Quotations' (1997)

56c77eedf86a10a6748dc8e20d096e4157085417.text:
Historical context
Source event: Source event not established.
Date: Unknown
Immediate context: The true source of personal satisfaction.

Meaning: Fulfillment is derived from productivity and the successful completion of demanding tasks, rather than from leisure or idleness.

Verification: Exact wording not verified
Source: Iain Dale (ed.), 'As I Said to Denis: The Margaret Thatcher Book of Quotations' (1997)

source.title: Jim Prior, 'A Balance of Power' (1986), p. 106

573412501ec88441938dae368acf42712f3952fd.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Source event not established.
Date: Unknown
Immediate context: During the late 1970s, Margaret Thatcher was shifting the Conservative Party away from the post-war consensus towards free-market policies. She frequently clashed with moderate Conservatives like Jim Prior over this ideological shift.

Meaning: Political compromise and centrist policies are inherently weak and leave a politician vulnerable to attacks from all ideological factions.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Jim Prior, 'A Balance of Power' (1986), p. 106

5816a59fb675d5765db15766fe8910246b9aa816.source_event: Article titled 'Why I'm Sure Britain Can Win'
5816a59fb675d5765db15766fe8910246b9aa816.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Article titled 'Why I'm Sure Britain Can Win'.
Date: September 22, 1974
Immediate context: The economic policies and egalitarian ideology of the Labour Party.

Meaning: Prioritizing the redistribution of wealth over its creation stifles economic growth and ultimately leads to universal impoverishment.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

5846d1f5edc27201f80031ef49263e6d7299b742.source_event: Speech to Scottish Conservative Party Conference
5846d1f5edc27201f80031ef49263e6d7299b742.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Scottish Conservative Party Conference.
Date: May 13, 1978
Immediate context: The failure of socialist economic policies and state intervention to create sustainable employment.

Meaning: Government spending programs only provide temporary illusions of employment; true, lasting jobs are the byproduct of a fundamentally sound and growing free-market economy.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Document 103681

586df70d0ca762e0c657a22adfee9caa7946da42.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Letter to the Daily Telegraph.
Date: August 21, 2001
Immediate context: Kenneth Clarke's suitability for the Conservative Party leadership.

Meaning: Kenneth Clarke's pro-European views and past record make him unfit to lead the party.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: The Daily Telegraph, August 21, 2001

5956332c9ec11e840051d9693954ea80ecc6d805.source_event: Address to Orpington Division Young Conservatives at Green-Street-Green
5956332c9ec11e840051d9693954ea80ecc6d805.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Address to Orpington Division Young Conservatives at Green-Street-Green.
Date: c. 1949
Immediate context: The contrast between state nationalisation and private ownership.

Meaning: Private ownership is essential to diffuse power and prevent the government from becoming more powerful than the citizens it serves.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation, Party Political Broadcast (BBC Radio 4)

596607c93f9aca406d8543ecc792e9a87fad0635.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Conservative Party Political Broadcast.
Date: 1975-03-05
Immediate context: The direction of British society and the Labour government's socialist agenda.

Meaning: The Labour Party's push towards a socialist society is dangerous and unrepresentative of the British public's desires, requiring a strong Conservative opposition to reverse the trend.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation, Party Political Broadcast (BBC Radio 4)

source.title: Margaret Thatcher Foundation archive, Speech to the Carlton Club

59b18840cbf67ac4a14a64f3858e7fcee40dfb48.text:
Historical context
Occasion: The Second Carlton Lecture.
Date: November 26, 1984
Immediate context: The spectrum of threats to British democracy and the rule of law.

Meaning: That violent terrorists and radical left-wing political factions, despite differing methods, both seek to subvert democratic institutions and the rule of law.

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation archive, Speech to the Carlton Club

5a4bdeaf484baa34fbbc226d2828b58fe98da975.source_event: Keith Joseph Memorial Lecture ('Liberty and Limited Government')
5a4bdeaf484baa34fbbc226d2828b58fe98da975.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Keith Joseph Memorial Lecture ('Liberty and Limited Government').
Date: January 11, 1996
Immediate context: The Labour Party's support for European federalism.

Meaning: Thatcher argued that the Labour Party supported European integration because it allowed them to impose socialist, interventionist policies through supranational institutions that they could no longer successfully implement through the British democratic process.

Verification: Normalised wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

5a7d71ca8c8a80423f1e3c5aabbc27479228e4ed.source_event: Speech to Conservative Central Council ('The Historic Choice')
5a7d71ca8c8a80423f1e3c5aabbc27479228e4ed.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Conservative Central Council ('The Historic Choice').
Date: March 20, 1976
Immediate context: The deceptive language of socialism.

Meaning: To argue that socialist policies do not deliver true justice but rather selectively punish success and enforce state control.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: margaretthatcher.org/document/102990

5ccc6c754f38343430f3ebc49a7903cce40b9ce8.source_event: Speech to Chilean businessmen in Santiago, Chile
5ccc6c754f38343430f3ebc49a7903cce40b9ce8.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Chilean businessmen in Santiago, Chile.
Date: March 21, 1994
Immediate context: The necessity of maintaining strong Western defense capabilities despite the end of the Cold War.

Meaning: Western democracies must not cut defense spending based on false optimism, but rather prepare for unpredictable future threats by maintaining military and technological superiority.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, THCR (March 21, 1994)

Verification: Historically verified variant
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

a9fad9cc9fc541d39017aabccaac1047f7079fb3.text:
Historical context
Occasion: Speech to Conservative Central Council.
Date: March 31, 1990
Immediate context: The failure of socialism in Eastern Europe and the contrast with Conservative policies.

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

Occasion: Speech celebrating the memory of Sir James Goldsmith.

Verification: Verified excerpt
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

Occasion: Speech to the American Enterprise Institute ("Re-learning old lessons").

Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive

Occasion: Speech to Conservative Party Conference ("Confrontation with reality").

Occasion: Speech to Conservative Central Council.

Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation archive, Interview for Hornsey Journal

Occasion: Speech to the Conservative Political Centre Summer School ('The Renewal of Britain').

Verification: Exact wording
Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Document 104107

Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive, Speech delivering Fourth Nicholas Ridley Memorial Lecture

Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation document 102990

Source: Margaret Thatcher Foundation Archive
